 Follow NJMVC urges residents to get Real ID before holidays
 Risha Inaganti, Cherry Hill Courier-Post Tue, November 10, 2026 at 10:18 AM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. With the holidays and year's end approaching, the New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission (NJMVC) is urging residents to get a Real ID.
 Real IDs have been required for adults to fly since May 2025.
 Appointments are available at NJMVC locations statewide. According to the NJMVC, appointment availability has expanded and wait times have decreased in comparison to the beginning of the year.
 Recent headlines: Walmart in Cinnaminson has grand reopening event 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Government should make people's lives easier," New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill said in a press release. "New Jerseyans were waiting an average of 73 days for a REAL ID appointment, and that was unacceptable. We made operational improvements at the MVC, and now residents can get an appointment in just three days as they prepare for holiday travel."
 Since the beginning of the year, the state has issued 750,000 Real IDs, the NJMVC said.
 How to get a Real ID in New Jersey 
 A Real ID is marked with a star symbol in the corner.
 Sample of a REAL ID in New Jersey To get a Real ID in New Jersey you will need the following:
 Two proofs of state residency. This can include a utility bill, bank statement or other forms of documentation.
 A valid Social Security number.
 Proof of identity. This can be a U.S. passport, birth certificate or other forms of identification.
 Advertisement Advertisement A full list of acceptable documentations can be found on the NJMVC's Real ID webpage .
 Once all the appropriate documents are found, a Real ID appointment can be made on the NJMVC's online scheduler .
 If you are within three months of the expiration date on your current license or identification, you can upgrade to a Real ID at your renewal appointment.
